According to preliminary information available so far, Nayak was heading towards his car accompanied by his bodyguard when the attack took place prompting the bodyguard to return fire in the direction of those who were shooting at them. The duo were not harmed in the incident.
The assailants are believed to have escaped by crossing the busy NH 66 Highway that leads into the state capital from the north.

Nayak, whose casino group operates two offshore casinos and several hotel casinos, is among the most prominent casino operators in the state and is popular among tourists.
A police official said that the investigations were at a preliminary stage and that it would be premature to comment on it.

On 26 August 2026, massive flash floods struck parts of Nepal and Tibet, causing widespread destruction as rivers including the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli overflowed and swept away homes, roads, bridges, and other infrastructure. Experts said the disaster was likely triggered by the collapse of a glacier and a massive ice-and-rock avalanche in the Himalayas, which sent huge amounts of debris and water into the river systems. As of 28 August 2026, the death toll in Nepal had risen to 469, according to Nepal Police, while nearly 1,000 people remained missing as search and rescue operations continued (here, here, and here).
Amid the disaster, multiple visuals are being shared on social media with the claim that they show visuals of the August 2026 Nepal floods. Let’s verify the truth behind these visuals in this article.
Claim: The visuals show the August 2026 Nepal floods.
Fact: None of the videos are related to the Nepal floods in August 2026. They are either old videos from other locations or AI-generated videos that are being shared as visuals of the disaster. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading.
Video 1
This video is being shared on social media with the claim that it shows a Chinese helicopter reaching the site where a glacier had broken, causing a massive amount of water to be released and resulting in widespread destruction in Nepal.
In our investigation, we found that the video was originally uploaded (archived) on the Instagram account of Leigh Coates, an American commercial helicopter pilot based in Valdez, Alaska. She posted the video on 22 August 2026 and specifically identified the location as Columbia Glacier in Alaska. She explained that a Jökulhlaup, also known as a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF), occurs when water trapped by glacier ice suddenly finds a way out, causing the water to drain rapidly beneath the glacier and rush downhill with immense force. She further stated that such events have been occurring annually at Columbia Glacier since 2014, although they are rarely captured because they generally occur in remote areas.
Video 2
The video is being shared on social media with claims that it shows the largest lake in the mountains whose embankment breached, causing the massive Nepal-Tibet floods.
We found that the video was uploaded by Leigh Coates on her official YouTube channel on 16 August 2026, before the Nepal floods. The video is titled “Before and After a Jökulhlaup Glacial Outburst Flood” and shows an example of the glacial outburst flood that occurred in Juneau, Alaska. This confirms that the video is unrelated to the August 2026 Nepal-Tibet floods.
Video 3
The video (here, here, and here) is being shared with claims on social media that it shows vehicles and buildings being swept away by flash floods in Nepal.
However, we found (archived) that this video has been available on the internet since 04 August 2026, at least 22 days before the Nepal floods. Moreover, upon examining the video, we noticed that the movement of the water and vehicles appeared unnatural.
We also analysed the video using AI detection tools such as Hive, which indicated that the video was AI-generated.
Video 4
This video is being shared with the claim that it shows vehicles being swept away by heavy floods during the August 2026 Nepal disaster.
We found that this video is related to the flash floods that occurred in the Chamoli region of Uttarakhand on 10 August 2026. Media reports (here, here) from the time also carried the same visuals and reported that vehicles were swept away after a bridge collapsed amid the flooding.
Video 5
This video is being shared with the claim that it shows a mudslide rapidly turning into a torrent of muddy floodwater during the August 2026 Nepal floods.
We found that the video is not related to the August 2026 Nepal floods. The video was actually recorded in Hpakant, Myanmar, in January 2024 (here, here).
Video 6
This video is being shared with the claim that it shows water and debris rushing down from a mountainous area and sweeping away homes during the August 2026 flash floods in Nepal.
We found (here, here, and here) that this video is from Dharali village in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand, and dates back to August 2025. It shows flash floods that occurred following a cloudburst in the upper catchment area of the Kheer Ganga River. The resulting floodwaters, debris and silt surged through Dharali, washing away houses and other structures. At least four people were confirmed dead, while more than 50 others were reported missing.
Video 7
This video is being shared with the claim that it shows a massive landslide occurring during the August 2026 Nepal floods.
We found (here, here) that this video has been available on the internet since at least 11 August 2026, predating the recent Nepal floods. Several users have claimed that the landslide was triggered by an earthquake that struck Colombia on 10 August 2026.
Video 8
This video is being shared with the claim that it shows a power plant being devastated amid the August 2026 Nepal floods. News outlets like NDTV, Dainik Bhaskar, and Divya Bhaskar also shared the video, claiming it was from Nepal.
We found (here, here, and here) that this video has been available online since at least 2022 and is not related to the August 2026 Nepal floods.
Video 9
This video is being shared with the claim that it shows people in Nepal running ahead of fast-moving floodwaters during the severe floods on 26 August 2026. Dainik Bhaskar, Punjab Kesari TV, and News18 Tamil Nadu also shared the video in the context of the Nepal floods.
We found that the video was available online as early as 04 August 2026, well before the 26 August 2026 Nepal floods, and therefore predates the disaster. The original post stated that the video showed rainfall in Yafa, a mountainous region of Yemen (here, here).
Video 10
The video (here, here) shows an elephant rescuing a man during the August 2026 Nepal floods.
We found that the video shows an elephant rescuing a man in Assam, India. The video was filmed several weeks before the August 2026 Nepal floods and is therefore unrelated to the disaster.
To sum up, none of these visuals are related to the Nepal floods in August 2026.

The story so far: The Union Health Ministry this past week tightened controls on all fixed-dose combinations (FDCs) containing chlorpheniramine maleate and phenylephrine hydrochloride, requiring manufacturers to carry a clear warning that they must not be used in children below four years of age.
What are these two drugs?
Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine. It can reduce allergy symptoms such as a runny nose and sneezing. Phenylephrine is a decongestant, intended to relieve a blocked nose.
An FDC puts both ingredients into one medicine. Such combinations are commonly encountered in cold/allergy preparations.
The government’s action does not mean every medicine containing either ingredient individually has been banned. The specific regulatory action concerns FDCs containing the two ingredients together.
What has changed now is the rule where manufacturers must put the warning. “Fixed Dose Combination shall not be used in children below four years of age” — on the label, package insert and promotional literature. The restriction covers manufacture, sale and distribution of these FDCs.
This expands an earlier action. In 2023, India’s Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) had already directed manufacturers of a particular chlorpheniramine + phenylephrine formulation to warn against use below four.
In April 2025, restrictions were imposed on certain FDCs. The August 2026 notification extends the warning requirement to all such formulations.
Why are children under four the focus?
Young children are more vulnerable to medication-related adverse effects because their bodies process medicines differently from adults and because dosing errors can have proportionally larger consequences.
The government’s Expert Committee and Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) concluded that these combinations could pose risks to children below four and that safer alternatives are available.
There is also a broader international concern around giving young children multi-ingredient cough-and-cold medicines. The US FDA, for example, warns that decongestant- or antihistamine-containing cough/cold products can cause serious adverse effects in very young children and notes the risk of accidental overdose when several ingredients are combined.
Does this mean cold medicines don’t work?
Not necessarily. These drugs can relieve symptoms, but they don’t cure the underlying viral infection. Most childhood colds resolve on their own. What doctors have been saying is that while parents may understandably want to make a congested or coughing child comfortable, but more medication isn’t automatically better.
For nasal congestion, relatively simple measures such as saline nasal drops/spray, fluids and a cool-mist humidifiercan help.
The key message is don’t self-medicate a child under four with a chlorpheniramine + phenylephrine combination, even if the product is marketed as a children’s cold medicine.
Check the active ingredients, not just the brand name. Many cold preparations contain several ingredients, creating a risk of accidentally giving the same drug twice through different products.
For fever or discomfort, parents should use medicines such as paracetamol/acetaminophen or ibuprofen only according to age/weight-appropriate instructions and medical advice.

For 26 days, India watched as Sonam Wangchuk wasted away. His hunger strike, held in solidarity with India’s “Cockroach” youth protest movement, would prove to be one of the most politically consequential fasts held in the country’s modern history.
Many in the country view the gruelling fast, which began on 28 June, as the crucial spark that helped propel the Cockroach movement into one of the most formidable challenges to the government of prime minister, Narendra Modi, in more than a decade.
Abhijit Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach movement, said Wangchuk had “awakened the conscience of an entire nation” through his sacrifice.
The Cockroach movement was launched in May, following the cancellation of a key nationwide exam to enter medical college after a paper was leaked. The cancellation was devastating for the 2 million students who had already sat the exam, a dozen of whom reportedly took their lives.
The movement took its name from comments made by India’s chief justice, Surya Kant, who had compared some unemployed young people to cockroaches and parasites in a court hearing.
Dipke’s demand for education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, to show accountability for the leak by resigning struck a nerve, and anger that had been seething below the surface surged out on to the streets.
The protest ballooned into a nationwide movement. For weeks, deadlock prevailed between the government and Dipke, backed by thousands who flocked to his sit-in protest in Delhi. Eventually, after an unprecedented police crackdown which further influenced public opinion in its favour, the protesters triumphed and Pradhan resigned on 25 July.
The victory was not a foregone conclusion and Dipke has acknowledged the importance of Wangchuck’s fast in determining the outcome. Unlike the students, Wangchuck was a well known and respected figure, recognised for his decades-long efforts to secure educational reforms and environmental protection. Last year, he was arrested in Ladakh on charges of inciting anti-government protests.
The timing was also key: crowds at the Delhi protest site had been thinning before he started his fast on a stage there on 28 June, injecting new energy and momentum into the movement.
Wangchuk had declared he would not end his strike until the government had listened to the demands of India’s protesting youth. He lay outdoors at the Cockroach protest site in the heart of Delhi, day and night, enduring rain, torturous heat and mosquitoes. Already a lean and slight figure, he lost 11kg over the 26 days.
“I felt confined, trapped … like a prison,” he told the Guardian. “The heat and humidity were awful.”
In the aftermath, Wangchuk, a softly-spoken engineer, environmentalist and educationist, remains humble about his role. “I was a known entity and that helped,” he said. His reverence is reserved for the hundreds of thousands of young people in the Cockroach movement, which he says has changed Indian politics for good.
Wangchuk is adamant that the Cockroach movement’s success is far bigger than a single resignation. In an era where dissent is routinely criminalised, young people, he said, had seized back the power of political protest.
“They have stripped away the curtain of fear that existed,” he said. “They are now engaged. They have tasted success in getting results and I expect them to continue.”
The 60-year-old admits the hunger strike took a gruelling toll. By the time he broke his fast on 24 July, he had pushed his body to the limit and was perilously close to organ failure. But as thousands of young people and politicians flocked to his side, his spirit remained unbroken throughout.
The greatest test, he says, came when he was forcibly removed by police from the protest site and taken to hospital against his will. Videos of his frail body being dragged away by burly police went viral and Wangchuk was hailed by young people online as a national hero. When mass protests erupted the following day, Wangchuk’s name was chanted and held aloft on placards.
Wangchuk was not always an obvious figure of anti-government resistance. Born in Ladakh, he rose to international prominence as an engineer and environmentalist, best known for inventing the ice stupor, a unique technique for water storage in human-made glaciers. He became a prominent champion of the rights of Ladakhis and set up his own school and cultural and environmental institution.
He had been a vocal supporter of several prominent policies of Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) but it soon turned to resistance as he accused the BJP of failing the people of Ladakh. Last year, as protests in Ladakh escalated, he was imprisoned by the government for almost six months under draconian anti-terrorist laws.
While his focus has been on rebuilding his body in recent weeks, regaining about 60% of his previous weight, Wangchuk has also continued his call for political reform, albeit without any overt criticism of the Modi government.
In a video message posted before India’s independence day in August, Wangchuk called for a “second independence movement” and urged Indians to choose men and women of “character and substance” to lead the country.
He has urged people to share the names of individuals of integrity who can be trusted and once he has a list, he plans to meet them in Mumbai and Delhi to discuss how elections can be cleansed of those with a criminal background.
“Indians have to trust those at the top,” he said. “At the moment, there is no trust in anything, not in elections, not in exams, not in civil servants. Clean and honest leaders are the first step to a better future.”
He expressed his support for the decision by the Cockroach movement to resist calls to become a political party and instead focus on being a pressure group, championing issues of education. “When we used to talk during the long days of the fast, I used to advise them that being a pressure group is the best way to keep clean and neutral,” he said.
For now, he is back living quietly in Ladakh, finally able to enjoy the one food that lingered on his mind during his hunger strike. “I did dream of apricots,” he said, “but that was just because I was wondering if mine back home had ripened.”

Story so far: The Supreme Court on August 20, 2026, has ruled that the police cannot independently investigate offences relating to illegal prenatal sex determination under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994. The responsibility lies primarily with the Appropriate Authority, a specialised body constituted under the law. In a judgment authored by a Bench of Justice Sanjay Karol and Justice Nongmeikapam Kotiswar Singh, it settles a long-standing disagreement among High Courts over whether the police could register FIRs and investigate such offences because they are classified as “cognisable” and “non-bailable”.
What was the case about?
The case arose from an allegation of illegal sex determination of a foetus at a hospital in Bulandshahar, Uttar Pradesh.
The District Magistrate, who was the Appropriate Authority under the Act, received information about the alleged practice. A Tehsildar was authorised to conduct a decoy operation. Following the operation, a raid was conducted at the hospital, and an FIR was registered against the doctor and others.
The FIR included offences under the Indian Penal Code as well as the sex-determination law. The accused approached the Allahabad High Court seeking to quash the chargesheet.
The High Court noticed that courts had taken different views on the role of the police in such cases and referred the issue to the Supreme Court.
There were essentially three questions before the Supreme Court: Can the police register an FIR for an offence under the Act? Can they investigate it? And can a Magistrate take cognisance of the offence on the basis of a police chargesheet?
Who is the Appropriate Authority?
The Appropriate Authority is the specialised authority created under the law to enforce the ban on sex selection and regulate the use of prenatal diagnostic techniques.
Section 17 of the Act specifically gives it the responsibility of investigating complaints of violations and taking action.
According to the section, when appointed for the whole of the State or the Union territory, it should consist of the following three members i) an officer of or above the rank of the Joint Director of Health and Family Welfare Chairperson; ii) an eminent woman representing women’s organisation; and iii) an officer of Law Department of the State or the Union territory concerned.
The functions of the appropriate authority includes to grant, suspend or cancel registration of a Genetic Counselling Centre, Genetic Laboratory or Genetic Clinic; to enforce standards prescribed for the Genetic Counselling Centre, Genetic Laboratory and Genetic Clinic; to investigate complaints of breach of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder and take immediate action and to seek and consider the advice of the Advisory Committee.
The Supreme Court therefore held that the law has deliberately placed the investigation of such offences with this specialised authority.
So, can the police register an FIR?
Not for the purpose of independently investigating a violation of the Act.
The complication came from Section 27 of the law, which says that every offence under it is “cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable.” A cognisable offence ordinarily allows the police to investigate without first obtaining permission from a court.
But the Supreme Court said that Section 27 cannot be read on its own. It has to be read along with the provisions that specifically give the Appropriate Authority the power to investigate and Section 28, which lays down how a court can take up an offence under the Act.
The Court said, “The language of the statute, more particularly Sections 27 and 28 of the Act when read together, in light of the other provisions and the socially beneficial nature of the Act as also the requirement of sensitivity along with medical and technical know-how, indicates that the police are not meant to be the investigators for the purpose of this Act. This is further made clear by the fact that an FIR once registered cannot be taken to its logical conclusion as per the procedures of this Act. The restriction applies only to offences under this Act and does not restrict the police’s power to investigate or prosecute independent offences disclosed under substantive criminal law (IPC/BNS)”.
The Court held that allowing the police to independently investigate would undermine this specialised system.
It said, “the police are not meant to be the investigators for the purpose of this Act.”
The police can, however, assist the Appropriate Authority when their help is necessary. Rule 18A(3)(iv) says that police involvement should be avoided “as far as possible”. The Court held that this rule has statutory force.
The phrase does leave room for police assistance, but not for an independent police investigation. The Court said that, when involved, the police would have to act “strictly in a supplemental or aiding capacity.”
What happens if there is also another crime?
The Supreme Court has not said that the police have no role whenever a suspected sex-determination offence is involved. The police can investigate a separate offence under the IPC, BNS or another criminal law, even if it arises from the same incident.
For example, if the facts disclose both a violation of the sex-determination law and an independently constituted offence under general criminal law, the two investigations can proceed separately.
The Appropriate Authority would investigate the offence under the special law. The police would investigate the independent criminal offence.
But the police cannot use the existence of another offence as a way of taking over the sex-determination investigation. The Court’s concurring opinion makes the distinction clear: the police cannot use a general criminal offence “as a gateway to take over the PC & PNDT inquiry.”
Similarly, the special law cannot be used to prevent the police from investigating a genuinely separate criminal offence.
Can a Magistrate act on a police chargesheet?
No. This was the third question before the Supreme Court, and the Court’s answer was categorical.
Section 28 says that a court cannot take cognizance of an offence under the Act except through the complaint mechanism specified in the provision. A police chargesheet therefore cannot, by itself, give the Magistrate jurisdiction to take cognizance of a PC &PNDT offence.
The Appropriate Authority has to follow the procedure prescribed under the Act.
The Court concluded that there is a “complete statutory embargo” on taking cognizance except in the situations provided under Section 28.
What is the takeaway?
The immediate impact is on how a suspected illegal sex-determination case moves through the criminal justice system.
If information received by a police station discloses only a violation under the Act, the police should record the information and send it, along with the relevant material, to the Appropriate Authority. They should not independently investigate the offence.
If the information also reveals an independent cognizable offence under the IPC, BNS or another general criminal law, the police can investigate that offence while sending the sex-determination component to the Appropriate Authority.
The Supreme Court has also made clear that a police investigation cannot simply end with a chargesheet for the offence under the Act. Section 28 creates a separate route for bringing such a case before a court.
The ruling does not weaken the prohibition on prenatal sex determination. Instead, it clarifies who is responsible for enforcing it.

Congress slams NCLT decision
A National Company Law Tribunal ruling that sharply reduced Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra’s liability in an insolvency case has sparked a political row
A National Company Law Tribunal ruling that sharply reduced Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra’s liability in a personal insolvency case has sparked a political row, with the Congress saying that a settlement of just ₹6.5 crore against lenders’ claims of more than ₹22,000 crore raises questions about the fairness of the process.
In a post on X, Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi called NCLT as “Neta-Company Loot Tribunal” and party general secretary Randeep Singh Surjewala said such reductions in debt value, called haircuts in financial parlance, amount to a loan waiver for industrialists. Neither leader, nor Congress’ communications chief Jairam Ramesh, who also raised the issue, named Chandra but referenced the NCLT decision.
A statement from Chandra’s office said that he has not borrowed from any lender in the matter and was only a personal guarantor for loans to companies”remotely connected” to the Essel Group. The total claims against him in the personal insolvency proceedings is only ₹3,992 crore and not ₹22,000 crore, the statement said. It also said a claim of ₹620 crore was settled and borrower entities have offered to pay ₹1,063 crore.
If a farmer doesn’t pay 50 thousand, his land gets auctioned off. If a salaried person misses even one EMI, bank goons show up at the house. Poor students can’t even get loans for education. But for select “friends,” bank money is like personal property - withdraw as much as you want, repay whatever you feel like. The Modi government has created two systems in the country - one for a handful of billionaires, and another for everyone else,” Gandhi said in his post.
“The tragedy of this country is that in name of haircuts, people are being pickpocketed. For pickpocketing, they devised a beautiful word called haircut. In name of haircut through NCLT this is an institutional loot and plunder of public and bank money by Modi government. These are words of late Prime Minister Manmohan Singh,” Congress general secretary Randeep Singh Surjewala said at a press conference.
“How can you have haircuts of 50 %, 60 %, 70 %, 80 %, 90 % and now 99 %? Then why are you having NCLT proceedings? This is loan waiver of industrialists in garb of haircuts. Congress Party has repeatedly raised this ...,” he added.
Ramesh claimed that haircut has become “mundan” (hair shaving).
“..The National Company Law Tribunal has just approved a repayment plan of a noted businessman under which creditors will receive only ₹6.5 crores against admitted claims of around ₹22,006.57 crore. This is not just a haircut. It is actually a mundan and makes a complete mockery of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016,” Ramesh posted on X.
Surjewala also demanded that “The finance minister must immediately come out of last 12 years’ data on how many lakh crores have been plundered in haircuts through NCLT? That figure may be upwards of Rs. 10 lakh crores, I suspect.”

Enough new coalmining projects were proposed last year to increase global supplies by 2.5bn tonnes a year, an increase of 11% from the year before, even as demand for coal plateaus, according to a new report.
Global Energy Monitor, an NGO, found that India ignited a rise in new coalmine proposals in 2025 despite a global slowdown in the number of mine openings because of falling demand for the fossil fuel.
The increase was driven almost entirely by the states of Jharkhand and Odisha, which doubled their proposals for new coalmines in line with an ambitious plan from India’s ministry of coal to increase the country’s output.
India plans to increase its coal production by nearly 100m tonnes to 1.15bn tonnes in the 2025-26 fiscal year to help meet the country’s rising demand for electricity to support economic growth and contend with heatwaves, which have become more severe and more frequent because of the climate crisis.
The planned increases come despite signs that the world is beginning to turn its back on coal in favour of renewable electricity, Global Energy Monitor said.
Coalmine proposals slowed in the years after the Covid-19 pandemic but have begun to climb again, raising concerns that mining could increase in the future despite a slowdown in the number of new facilities.
The startup of new coalmining projects has fallen steadily in recent years, according to the Global Energy Monitor’s latest report.
It found that enough new coalmines to produce about 113m tonnes each year began operations last year, down by 40% from 2024, which was already the lowest annual total in a decade.
This was largely owing to a slowdown in new mines in China and Australia, which fell by 44% and 96% respectively.
Global Energy Monitor warned that India’s rise in new mine proposals was at odds with the slowdown in global coal demand predicted by the International Energy Agency for the end of the decade.
Wind and solar power surpassed coal generation in the global electricity mix for the first time last year, according to a separate report from energy thinktank Ember, in a “milestone moment” for climate action.
China and India were largely responsible for the rise in renewables, according to the Ember report, while the US and Europe continued to rely more heavily on fossil fuels.
Tiffany Means, a senior researcher at Global Energy Monitor and co-author of the report said: “The economic rationale for expanding coalmining becomes progressively weaker as low-cost clean energy continues to displace coal.
“Rather than locking in decades of additional coal production, governments have an opportunity to cancel projects that remain in the development pipeline before they advance to construction.”

Doctors from a private health facility in West Bengal have successfully treated a seven- year-old boy suffering from thalassaemia using an advanced Haplo Cord transplant process.
The parents of the 7-year-old child diagnosed with HbE Beta thalassemia, who needs monthly blood transfusions, were counseled to register under the “Save the Sibling” programme. They underwent IVF (in vitro fertilization) and pre-implantation genetic testing to produce a matched thalassemia-free sibling with compatible HLA (human leukocyte antigen), which is critical for bone marrow transplantation.
A haplo-cord transplant was performed using the cord blood from the patient’s sibling and some stem cells from his father. The transplant was conducted by Narayana Health. During the transplant period, the child developed complications such as infections, mucositis, liver derangement, and persistent low blood counts, which were effectively managed. The patient has recovered well and is now transfusion-free, the doctors said.
In another feat, the team treated a 62-year-old male patient from Myanmar with brain cancer after a successful CAR T-cell therapy (an advanced type of immunotherapy). The patient was initially found to be having gait disturbance (an unusual change in the way a person walks). He was then diagnosed to have primary CNS lymphoma, a rare, aggressive type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma where cancer cells form in the brain, spinal cord, cerebrospinal fluid, or eyes.
After receiving four cycles of high-dose chemotherapy yielding unsatisfactory results, the doctors decided to have him undergo CAR T-cell therapy. He underwent lymphocyte collection, bridging with radiation and other medications, before receiving a dual CAR targeting CD19 and CD22 on the cancer cells.
Speaking about these two rare recoveries, Joydeep Chakrabartty, Senior Consultant, Hemato Oncology & Clinical Lead - BMT Programme (East), Narayana Health, said that the recoveries are landmark achievements with both facing potential fatalities.
“Using the Haplo-cord technology for the child and the CAR T-cell therapy for the aged patient, the expert team of doctors attending them have been able to turn their lives around for the better. Narayana Health has always been at the forefront in breaking new grounds in medical science, and these two cases clearly reflect that,” Dr. Chakrabartty said.
Also read: Evidence of CAR T-cell therapy against cancers presented at US conference
Prasanta Chowdhury, Laboratory Director, Cord Life Sciences India Pvt. Limited, said that cord blood banking is a complex issue involving medical, financial, ethical, and scientific debates. “The core dilemma centres on choosing between private storage for family use and public donation for general use, weighed against high costs and low statistical odds of personal use. In these two cases, we have successfully addressed every single concern with absolute compassion and clarity,” Dr. Chowdhury said.

In short:
Crown Prince Haakon has become the king of Norway after the death of his father, Harald V.
Harald died at Oslo University Hospital on Friday at the age of 89.
What's next?
King Haakon VIII will have the task of boosting popular support for the royal family, which has suffered reputational blows in recent years.
Norway has a new king, whose tasks will include stabilising its monarchy and boosting the royal family's popularity after his wife's past contacts with deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his stepson's rape conviction.
Crown Prince Haakon, 53, became King Haakon VIII when his father Harald V died on Friday at the age of 89.
Haakon adopted the motto, "All for Norway," that dates back to his great-grandfather.
His wife became Queen Mette-Marit, while his oldest child became Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra and the heir to the throne.
In recent years Haakon has stepped in as his aging father's health began to fail.
Loading...
Norway's monarchy has old roots, tracing its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the 9th century.
When Norway regained its independence from Sweden in 1905 three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy.
Today, the role is largely symbolic as the power lies with an elected parliament, but the country's royal family retains celebrity and a role in promoting the wealthy nation around the world.
Royal family looks to rebuild reputation
One task for the new king will be to shore up popular support for the royal family, which has suffered blows to its reputation in recent years.
Haakon is the younger child of Harald, born two years after his sister, Princess Märtha Louise.
As the oldest male, however, he became heir to the throne when his grandfather, King Olav, died in 1991.
The Norwegian Constitution was altered in 1990 to allow future firstborns, regardless of gender, to take precedence in the line of succession. However, it was not applied retroactively.
Haakon holds a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of California at Berkeley and a master's degree in development studies from the London School of Economics and Political Science, with a specialisation in international trade and Africa.
In 1995 he graduated from the Royal Norwegian Naval Academy, and he also completed the foreign ministry's trainee program for diplomats.
An avid surfer, skier and sportsman, he told Norwegian broadcaster NRK that if he had not been a royal he would have been a surfer.
A music lover, he likes rock and rap, he attended festivals across Europe as a youth.
New king married a single mother
Haakon sought the king's permission to marry, under unique circumstances, before he wed in August 2001 at Oslo Cathedral.
Haakon knew his relationship would face an uphill battle for acceptance when he met Mette-Marit Tjessem Høiby at a popular music festival in Norway in 1999.
She was a single mother whose son's father had been sentenced to prison for cocaine possession, and she had been seen at parties where illegal drugs were used.
They have two children, Ingrid Alexandra and Prince Sverre Magnus.
Haakon also became the stepfather of Mette-Marit's son, Marius Borg Høiby, who has no royal title.
The royal family's reputation took a hit from his stepson's trial
In June, Marius Borg Høiby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of rape. He was found guilty of two of the four rape charges he was facing and acquitted of the other two.
He was also convicted of assault and abuse in a close relationship. Høiby's lawyers said he will appeal the convictions.
The trial unfolded amid renewed scrutiny of the royal family following disclosures about Mette-Marit's past contacts with Jeffrey Epstein, the deceased sex offender.
She has publicly apologised for the association and said she exercised poor judgement in maintaining contact with him. She is not accused of any wrongdoing.
In a television interview in March she said she was manipulated and deceived by Epstein and felt unsafe during a 2013 encounter with him at his Palm Beach, Florida, mansion.
Harald 'much-loved' king
Britain's King Charles has joined the tributes to King Harald, who ruled for 35 years "with warmth and humility".
"As Norway mourns the loss of so towering a figure, my whole family join in remembering a much-loved kinsman and friend," King Charles said in a statement.
"[His] kindness, compassion and deep sense of duty echoed from across the sea and across the decades.
"The queen and I extend our deepest and most heartfelt condolences to Queen Sonja and all her family as Britain shares in Norway's grief at this time of such heartbreaking loss."
Pope Leo spoke of King Harald's "devoted service" which he hoped would "continue to bear fruit".
"I offer the assurance of my prayers for the eternal rest of the late king," Pope Leo said.
"Upon the Norwegian people and all who mourn his loss I cordially invoke almighty God's blessings of consolation and peace."
Manchester City's Norwegian World Cup star Erling Haaland said he hoped Harald would "rest in peace".
"Thank you for everything you meant to Norway. It was an honour to meet you,"

Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) Director John Ratcliffe, who on Tuesday, August 25, made an unannounced visit to Moscow, has shared his bleak assessment of the state of the Russia-Ukraine war with is Russian counterparts, The New York Times has reported. Ratcliffe made the secretive visit to Moscow amid reports that Russia was planning to attack a NATO member country, most likely Poland, even as the war with Ukraine drags on.
The Wall Street Journal and CBS News reported CIA Director Ratcliffe's visit was aimed to dissuade Russia from attacking NATO members.
The New York Times report added that Ratcliffe met Aleksandr V. Bortnikov, the head of Russia’s FSB intelligence service, and urged the Russians to cut a deal before their military and economic situation gets worse.
Ratcliffe's Moscow visit
Ratcliffe, a longtime Russia hawk, is one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit Russia since its war with Ukraine started in 2022. His predecessor, William Burns, had made a trip to Moscow in November 2021, just months before Russia launched its special military operation in Ukraine, in an effort to dissuade Putin from going ahead with the invasion, which is now its fifth year.
The special military operation in Ukraine, which Russia estimated to last just a handful of days, has so far killed hundreds of thousands, and despite it inflicting a high cost, the Kremlin has refused to ease its maximalist demands of keeping Crimea, which it occupied in 2014, and full control of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia, which it partly controls now.
CIA analysts have long questioned whether Putin’s advisers have given him honest assessments of the war’s trajectory and toll.
Ratcliffe discussed Iran war
According to the NYT report, the CIA has long maintained communications channels with the FSB and Russia’s foreign intelligence service, SVR.
The report added that Ratcliffe made no threats about potential consequences for the Russian side should President Vladimir Putin ignore the CIA director’s assessment and choose to continue fighting.
CBS News reported that during his visit, Ratcliffe also discussed the war with Iran, warning of additional sanctions if the Strait of Hormuz doesn't reopen to shipping traffic.
Meanwhile, on Thursday, Sergei Naryshkin, the head of Russia's SVR, confirmed that he had held a "working-level meeting" with Ratcliffe in Moscow where they discussed unspecified and sensitive matters falling within the remit of their respective intelligence services.
Trump, Kremlin deny NATO attack plan
The Kremlin has also dismissed as "scare stories" US media reports suggesting that Russia could attack NATO.
"A lot of such scare stories are being published right now. Of course, they have nothing to do with reality," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
US President Donald Trump on Thursday also expressed confidence that Russia would not attack NATO territory.
"I've had good talks with him. He's not going to be attacking a NATO territory," Trump told reporters at the White House when asked if Putin had agreed not to do so.

Sarfaraz denies knowing about Pakistan threat to end tour
- Published
Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said he and his players did not know about a Pakistan Cricket Board threat to the England and Wales Cricket Board over a Sky interview with the sons of Imran Khan.
During lunch on day one of the second Test, Sky Sports aired an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran, who has been in prison for the past three years.
It is understood the PCB raised the prospect of cancelling the Test at Lord's and the remainder of the three-match tour if the interview aired.
A version of the interview was broadcast, and the players returned to the field after the interval to continue the match.
"I don't know anything. I'm just focusing on the match," said Sarfaraz at the end of the second day's play.
"You're talking about the interview? We don't know about the interview."
Asked if there was ever a possibility his players would return for the afternoon session on day one, the former Pakistan wicketkeeper said: "All are OK. We were having lunch at that time."
Legendary all-rounder Imran Khan, 73, had a 21-year international career for Pakistan and famously led his team to World Cup glory in 1992.
He served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022. Since 2023, Khan has been in jail on corruption charges which he denies.

The PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi also serves as Pakistan's interior minister.
In the interview conducted by former England captain Michael Atherton, Suleiman and Kasim expressed concerns over the treatment and security given to their father, as well as criticising the UK government's response.
Before it aired, Sky received a complaint about the plan to broadcast the interview.
In response to the tension around the situation, the ECB took government advice from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
In Pakistan, the match is being aired by the public broadcaster PTV, using Sky's pictures. PTV did not air the interview.
Ultimately, the tourists resumed play after lunch and the Test has continued to the end of the second day, with England 261 runs ahead at 81-3 in their second innings.
It is understood Sky received no further complaints on Friday in relation to the interview.
In October, England will tour Pakistan for a one-day tri-series against the home side and Sri Lanka.
It will be England's fourth separate tour of Pakistan in the past four years following a 17-year gap between visits to the country because of security concerns.
In 2006, a Test between England and Pakistan at The Oval was abandoned after the visitors were accused of ball tampering.
Pakistan were adjudged to have forfeited the match after refusing to play after tea on the fourth day, the only instance in Test history when a team has forfeited a Test.

A video showing a man grabbing a young man by the collar, slapping him in a crowded area, and attacking him with a banana plant is being widely shared on social media (here, here, here) with the claim that a BJP MLA from Assam assaulted a man while attending a bridge inauguration ceremony. Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: Video of a man being assaulted by an Assam BJP MLA during a bridge inauguration ceremony.
Fact: This video shows Samsul Huda, the All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) MLA from Bilasipara East in Assam’s Dhubri district, allegedly assaulting an employee of a construction company during a bridge foundation stone-laying ceremony in March 2025. Hence, the claim made in the post is MISLEADING.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a video report published on Munsif TV’s YouTube channel on 20 March 2025. The video was captioned, “AIUDF MLA Samsul Huda Loses Temper During Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony in Bilasipara.”
A keyword search also led us to media reports about the same incident (here, here). According to these reports, Samsul Huda, the All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) MLA from Bilasipara East in Assam’s Dhubri district, had attended a bridge foundation stone-laying ceremony, where he allegedly assaulted an employee of the construction company. The incident took place on 18 March 2025 and triggered widespread public outrage across Dhubri district.
To sum up, an old video of AIUDF MLA Samsul Huda assaulting a man is being falsely shared as a BJP MLA’s attack.

Serial killers and child abductions. Trippy science-fiction stories about alternate realities. A courtroom drama starring an anthropomorphic coyote with more than a passing resemblance to Who Framed Roger Rabbit? Screwball comedies, dark horror flicks and so much more await in this weekend’s edition of your friendly neighborhood streaming guide.

New TV Shows To Watch This Weekend
Adults – Season 2 (Hulu)

FXX is also airing two episodes each Thursday, which puts the linear finale on September 17.
Why You Should Watch: This isn’t one I’ve watched yet, but the reviews are through the roof. Critics give Season 2 a 100% score and audiences are almost right there with them at 98%. If you’re looking for something funny to kill some time this weekend, give it a look.
Dark Matter – Season 2 (Apple TV)
What It’s About: Joel Edgerton returns as physicist Jason Dessen alongside Jennifer Connelly as Daniela and Oakes Fegley as their son Charlie, with Alice Braga, Jimmi Simpson, Dayo Okeniyi and Amanda Brugel also returning. After the first season’s multiverse chaos, the Dessens attempt to settle in a seemingly safe reality while Jason’s obsession with the Box threatens to drag the family straight back into trouble. New episodes drop Fridays, though on Apple TV this actually means Thursday evenings, with the finale October 30 (or 29, as the case may be).

Now Crouch moves into uncharted territory, taking his own story further in TV format than in book format, which is kind of cool and unique and hopefully means we’re in for a great second season. The good news? Season 2 has much higher ratings than Season 1 so far.

What It’s About: A fun new Disney+ exclusive Simpsons special that very deliberately riffs on Black Mirror (if that wasn’t totally obvious by the title). Demi Moore and Patti Harrison guest star.
Why You Should Watch: I suppose if you’re a fan of both The Simpsons and Black Mirror, this is a no-brainer. I always liked The Simpsons Halloween episodes and this is kind of the same vibe. I haven’t really watched The Simpsons in ages, and I can only do Black Mirror in very small doses but I might still check this special out.
Revival – Season 1 (Netflix)
What It’s About: This supernatural mystery is based on the Image Comics series by Tim Seeley and Mike Norton and was adapted for TV by Luke Boyce and Aaron B. Koontz. Melanie Scrofano stars as Wisconsin deputy Dana Cypress, whose small town is thrown into chaos when recently deceased residents suddenly return to life—not as shambling zombies, but apparently as the same people they were before they died. The series originally aired on Syfy back in 2025 and just dropped all 10 episodes on Netflix.
Why You Should Watch: This one has two things going for it. First, the first season basically tied up the storylines from the comics, meaning that even if there’s never a second season, you have a pretty complete story here. Second, the reviews are very strong: 90% critics and 85% audiences on Rotten Tomatoes.
The Undeclared War – Season 2 (Peacock)
What It’s About: The British cyber-thriller returns with Simon Pegg as GCHQ operations director Danny Patrick and Hannah Khalique-Brown as Saara Parvin. Following the devastating Russian cyberattack of Season 1, the GCHQ team discovers evidence of a mole while a new Chinese cyber threat begins targeting the British government. Siân Brooke joins a returning cast that also includes Adrian Lester, Alex Jennings and Danny Sapani.
Why You Should Watch: The entire season is out now on Peacock so if you haven’t seen Season 1 yet, you could just binge both seasons all at once. It’s an interesting premise, though reviews peg (get it?) the show at around 67% on RT – a passable, if not tremendous, “Fresh” score.
New Movies To Watch This Weekend
The Whisper Man (Netflix)
What It’s About: Adam Scott stars as Tom Kennedy, a widowed crime novelist whose 8-year-old son is abducted, forcing him to seek help from his estranged father, Peter Willis (Robert De Niro), a retired detective whose decades-old serial-killer investigation may be connected to the disappearance. Michelle Monaghan plays detective Amanda Beck, with Hamish Linklater and Owen Teague also starring.
Why You Should Watch: Adam Scott, Robert De Niro, Michelle Monaghan, Hamish Linklater, Owen Teague. I mean, that’s one helluva cast! And the premise is certainly intriguing. I’m a sucker for serial killer mysteries and Adam Scott is always a joy to watch. This is definitely going on my weekend watch-list, though I’m so busy this weekend I’m not sure I’ll have time to watch anything I’m not already reviewing!
The Woman In The Yard (Peacock)
What It’s About: Danielle Deadwyler stars as Ramona, a grieving mother recovering from the accident that killed her husband while trying to raise their two children alone in an isolated farmhouse. Then a mysterious woman dressed in black simply appears in the yard—and begins moving closer to the house.
Why You Should Watch: It sounds spooky and everyone loves a good horror movie these days, but the 41% RT score is a red flag, and I’m not sure it’s my cup of tea. But maybe it’s yours!
Borderlands (Peacock)
What It’s About: The infamous video-game adaptation stars Cate Blanchett as Lilith, Kevin Hart as Roland, Ariana Greenblatt as Tiny Tina, Jamie Lee Curtis as Tannis and Jack Black as the voice of Claptrap. Eli Roth directed the film, which follows the mismatched group across Pandora while searching for the missing daughter of powerful corporate magnate Atlas.
Why You Should Watch: I might watch it just because it’s streaming now, but this movie has looked terrible from the very first time I saw stills. Things were far more grim than even I predicted, and the movie currently has a 10% Rotten Tomatoes score! 10%! It was a huge critical and financial failure despite the big names attached and earned less than $16 million at the box office on a budget topping $110 million. Talk about a flop! Flop slop! I kind of want to watch it with some friends MST3000 style.
M3GAN (Netflix)
What It’s About: Allison Williams stars as roboticist Gemma, who suddenly becomes guardian to her orphaned niece Cady (Violet McGraw) and decides that pairing the girl with her experimental AI companion doll M3GAN will solve both her parenting and work problems. Predictably, an AI whose overriding directive is protecting a child begins interpreting “protection” rather aggressively. Amie Donald physically portrays M3GAN, with Jenna Davis providing the voice.
Why You Should Watch: This movie is a few years old now and there’s already a sequel and probably three more movies planned and the eventual reboot is already a twinkle in some movie producer’s eye, but I liked this little comedy-horror picture when it came out and you should give it a watch if you’re looking for something light and a little weird.
Venom: The Last Dance (Netflix)
What It’s About: Tom Hardy returns for the third and supposedly final outing as Eddie Brock and his symbiote alter ego Venom. This time they're being hunted simultaneously by government forces led by Chiwetel Ejiofor's Rex Strickland and a monstrous Xenophage sent by symbiote god Knull, voiced/performed by Andy Serkis. Juno Temple, Rhys Ifans and Stephen Graham round out the cast.
Why You Should Watch: Talk about a stacked cast for what is almost certainly a mediocre movie. I’ve only seen the first of the Tom Hardy Venom movies, unless I’ve simply forgotten watching the second one. Audiences liked this quite a bit more than critics (79% Popcornmeter vs 40% critic score). I liked the first Venom movie more than I expected but not really enough to continue following the series.
The Last Sunrise (Prime Video)
What It’s About: Maia Reficco stars as Oriah “Ry,” a young American dancer who travels to Mallorca with her mother (Eva Longoria) and falls for local fisherman Julián, played by Fernando Lindez. Their Mediterranean romance becomes complicated when Ry's mother becomes involved in a resort development threatening Julián's family's land.
Why You Should Watch: I mean, Mallorca sounds nice this time of year. I’d like to go. This film sounds about as far from something I’d actually watch as you can get, but I know some of you enjoy this kind of romance, so here you go. Have at it!
New Movies In Theaters This Weekend
Coyote vs Acme
What It’s About: Wile E. Coyote (of Looney Tunes fame) finally decides he’s had enough of being maimed by defective ACME products and hires ambulance-chasing attorney Kevin Avery (Will Forte) to sue the company. John Cena plays ACME’s attorney. It’s a courtroom comedy involving an anthropomorphic coyote, basically.
Why You Should Watch: This is a bit of a miracle movie. Warner Bros. finished the movie and decided to not release it in order to claim a tax write-off, a practice they did with a number of movies and shows (along with other studios, including Disney). There was major backlash and Warner Bros. sold the film to Ketchup Entertainment. It now sits at 95% on Rotten Tomatoes with critics and 92% with audiences, making it one of the best-reviewed entries in this guide, and hopefully makes a bundle of cash for its rescuers.
The Dog Stars
What It’s About: Ridley Scott directs this post-apocalyptic adaptation of Peter Heller's novel, starring Jacob Elordi as Hig, a pilot surviving after a pandemic alongside hardened survivalist Bangley (Josh Brolin). A mysterious radio transmission sends Hig beyond their isolated compound, eventually bringing him into contact with characters played by Margaret Qualley and Guy Pearce. Allison Janney and Benedict Wong also star.
Why You Should Watch: Ridley Scott, a stellar cast, a cool post-apocalyptic setting and . . . well, Ridley Scott. Scott has been putting out dud after dud after dud, and this one appears to be yet another, with just a 40% RT score. Actually, when I saw the trailer for the first time I thought “Wow, this looks really cool” and then I saw who directed it and immediately was reminded of how much I hated Gladiator II. What a shame.
TV Shows Currently Streaming Weekly
Reacher – Season 4 (Prime Video)
What It’s About: Season 4 of Reacher adapts Lee Child’s Gone Tomorrow: a distraught woman’s death on a Philadelphia subway pulls Jack Reacher (Alan Ritchson) into a conspiracy involving the Pentagon and an international terror cell. Three episodes dropped August 12, with weekly releases through the September 16 finale. Amazon will release all eight episodes of the spinoff Neagley (starring Maria Sten) the same day as the finale.
Why You Should Watch: Season 1 remains the gold standard when it comes to Reacher, but at least Season 3 was a lot better than the truly atrocious second season of this action-crime-mystery-ish adaptation of the over-the-top Lee Child books (of which I’ve read about nine or so). I finally posted my review of the season (so far) and . . . the verdict is not pretty. I’m not even getting much pushback on my criticism, with many fans very unhappy with how the season is shaping up. You can watch my video discussion of the season right here.
Lanterns – Season 1 (HBO Max)
What It’s About: DC’s True Detective-style take on Green Lantern: rookie John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and veteran Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) investigate a Nebraska murder that opens onto something much larger, told across two timelines. Kelly Macdonald is Sheriff Kerry, Ulrich Thomsen plays Sinestro, Laura Linney a Guardian of the Universe, and Nathan Fillion reprises Guy Gardner from Superman. Co-created by Chris Mundy (Ozark), Damon Lindelof, and Tom King. Premieres Sunday, August 16 at 9pm, then weekly across eight episodes, with the finale on October 4. See the full release schedule and time zones right here.
Why You Should Watch: I’ve watched the first episode of Lanterns so far and it’s fine. Nothing special, not bad, I’m curious about the mystery though I think they did a pretty terrible job at actually setting that mystery up in the pilot. You can read my review of the Season 1 premiere and my review of Episode 2, and I’ll be recapping and reviewing episodes weekly on Sunday evenings, though as I note in that second link, I think this probably should have just been a binge release.
Furious – Season 1 Finale on Monday (Hulu)
What It’s About: An eight-episode crime drama created by Elizabeth Meriwether, loosely inspired by the 1987 film Black Widow. FBI agent Alice Black (Emmy Rossum) hunts a calculating female serial killer played by Lola Petticrew (who I first saw in Say Nothing, I believe). As their paths converge the line between justice and revenge gets blurry. Scoot McNairy, Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Jake Lacy also star. If you’re enjoying this show, the good news is that Season 2 has already been greenlit ahead of the Season 1 finale.
Why You Should Watch: I have decidedly mixed feelings about Furious as we approach the finale. I think part of this is marketing. The show is described as a rookie FBI agent hunting down a female serial killer, but it’s really about a revenge killer and abuse and sex trafficking and I guess I was just hoping it wouldn’t be so predictable. I don’t love how often modern shows and movies give female serial killers a “pass” by justifying their murders because of past abuse. I purely evil female serial killer would be a nice change. Men shouldn’t get to have all the fun. Still, cat-and-mouse serial killer detective shows are one of my guilty pleasures so I’ll be watching this on Monday nights. The finale will arrive furiously on August 31.
It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia – Season 18 (FX / Hulu)
What It’s About: The Gang — Charlie Day, Glenn Howerton, Rob Mac, Kaitlin Olson and Danny DeVito — return to Paddy’s Pub for a 10-episode run that includes inheritance scams, tent encampments, workplace automation, neurodivergence, conspiracy theories, a Renaissance Faire, and a Little League sponsorship. What could go wrong? The season premiered this past Monday, August 17 with a two-episode drop. Weekly episodes land on Mondays with the finale airing on October 12. Season 18 is currently sitting at 100% on Rotten Tomatoes.
Why You Should Watch: To be fair, I’m late to the game on Always Sunny, so I’m way way behind on this show and just put on episodes whenever I need a dose of hilarity in my life. Sometimes I end up binging three or four or five because life is filled with tragedy and the Gang always lifts my spirits. So why should you watch? First, because it will bring you joy. Second, because you’ll be like “there but for the grace of God go I.”
The Shards (Hulu)
What It’s About: Ryan Murphy (Glee, The Politician, etc) adapts the Bret Easton Ellis novel of the same name for FX/Hulu. Set in Los Angeles in 1981, The Shards follows a 17-year-old fictionalized Bret Easton Ellis (Igby Rigney) through his senior year at the elite Buckley prep school, where the arrival of enigmatic transfer student Robert Mallory (Homer Gere) coincides with the killings of a serial murderer known as The Trawler. The show drops new episodes on Wednesdays with a September 9 finale.
Why You Should Watch: I’m not really sure, if we’re being honest. The promo images of young people in the 80s in swimsuits make this look like a show for young people and I’m not a young man anymore. The reviews aren’t great (55% / 35% audience and critic scores) and I suppose I’m not really a big Bret Easton Ellis guy. I mean, I enjoyed the movie American Psycho, but I never read the book! Maybe I should do that instead of watching this show.
The Walking Dead: Dead City – Season 3 (AMC+)
What It’s About: The Walking Dead: Dead City returns with an eight-episode season 3, with Lauren Cohan as Maggie Rhee and Jeffrey Dean Morgan as Negan returning, now working alongside Perlie Armstrong (Gaius Charles) to build a "functioning" community in post-apocalyptic Manhattan. The fragile alliance is tested by newcomer Renata (Aimee Garcia), her doctor brother Luis (Raúl Castillo), and loner Dillard (Jimmi Simpson of Westworld fame). New showrunner Seth Hoffman, a Walking Dead veteran writer and former co-executive producer on the original series, is taking over this season. New episodes drop Sundays, running through September 13.
Why You Should Watch: I don’t think this show should exist, quite frankly, and after watching the Season 3 premiere, I not only wrote a scathing review, I made a scathing video to go with it, which you can watch here. It’s not good, folks, but I genuinely hope that it gets better because there are other ways I could be spending my Sunday evenings. Update: I watched about five minutes of the second episode and turned it off and I haven’t been able to come back. I think maybe you need alcohol to enjoy this show, or to even enjoy hate-watching this show, and I don’t drink anymore.
Fightland (Starz)
What It’s About: On the night Maduka "Duke" Kilroy (Howard Charles) becomes world heavyweight champion, an assault leaves his brother dead and lands him in a U.S. prison for eight years. Out and back in London, he sets out to destroy the empire of criminal kingpin and former promoter Kingsley Marshall (Nicholas Pinnock), the man he blames — complicated by the fact that Kingsley has vanished and his wife Joy (Deborah Ayorinde) is the love of Duke’s life. Charles Babalola and Anita-Joy Uwajeh co-star. New episodes drop Fridays with the season finale landing on September 25.
Why You Should Watch: I’m a few weeks late to this – it premiered on Starz on July 31. In any case, it’s co-produced by rapper Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson, marking his first international series. It’s a pretty compelling plot and has a reasonably strong 73% on Rotten Tomatoes. Also, boxing. Boxing is fun especially when the boxer in question is beating up criminals in East London.
Ted Lasso – Season 4 (Apple TV)
What It’s About: Ted Lasso (Jason Sudeikis) returns to Richmond to coach a second-division women’s football team in this reboot of the popular Apple TV sports comedy series. Jack Burditt (30 Rock, Modern Family) takes over as showrunner for this new, more estrogen-charged spin on the fish-out-of-water TV show. New episodes drop on Wednesday (Tuesday evening for Apple TV) with ten episodes running through October 7.
Why You Should Watch: Honestly, the reason that Ted Lasso worked so well in the first season was precisely because it was a fish-out-of-water comedy. But a fish can only stay out of water for so long before, well, RIP fish. Ted was an adorable lead and head coach and despite his lack of experience or knowledge of soccer, his remarkable way with people took everyone off guard, including viewers. That affable, mustachioed man was the epitome of “I am rubber and you are glue” and nothing stuck to him. He made you want to believe (like Fox Mulder did back int he day, only about aliens and whatnot). 
That rarest work of optimism and hope in a sea of cynicism was perfect in its first season. But it should have been a one-and-done series because it ran out of steam in Season 2 and I didn’t return for Season 3. Let me know if you think Season 4 is worth it or a misfire. I’ve heard mixed things.
Monsters of God (HBO Max)
What It’s About: A five-part HBO documentary series directed by Eric Goode (Tiger King, Chimp Crazy), produced by Goode Films, A24, and Central Pictures. Goode dives into the underworld of exotic animal smuggling, a billion-dollar criminal enterprise driven by obsession over rare species. The docuseries is inspired by and draws from the 2008 nonfiction book, The Lizard King, by Bryan Christy (oddly, not about The Doors frontman, Jim Morrison). New episodes drop Mondays with a September 3 finale.
Why You Should Watch: I really think Lizard King would have been a better name for this series, since it would so quickly evoke Goode’s hit Tiger King, but maybe that name was taken or maybe they worried about the link to The Doors. Either way, with a 100% Rotten Tomatoes score (based on just 10 reviews) this one might be worth checkikng out. 
Conan O’Brien Must Go – Season 3 (HBO Max)
What It’s About: Conan travels overseas to meet listeners he first connected with on his podcast, experiencing local traditions while spending time with the fans who invited him — this season to India, the Philippines, the Netherlands and Morocco. Premieres Friday, August 21 at 9 pm ET on HBO and HBO Max with four episodes airing weekly on Fridays, and the finale on September 11.
Why You Should Watch: Conan O’Brien is just one of the funniest, most likable people in Hollywood and basically anything he does is worth watching just because he’s such a fun guy. If you like humorous travel shows, check it out. The series holds 88% critics / 84% audience and has won two Emmys.
Star Trek: Strange New Worlds – Season 4 (Paramount+)
What It’s About: The crew of the U.S.S. Enterprise is back for another round of adventures as Captain Christopher Pike (Anson Mount) continues leading his crew across the final frontier. Season 4 picks up after last season’s cliffhanger and sends Pike, Spock, Number One, and the rest of the Enterprise crew on a series of dangerous new missions, from mysterious alien encounters to impossible scientific mysteries, while continuing to build toward the events of Star Trek: The Original Series. The new season is comprised of 10 episodes airing Sundays through September 24
Why You Should Watch: I actually gave up on New Star Trek some time ago, having doggedly tried my best with the JJ Abrams films, Discovery and Picard. And while I’d heard some very positive things about Strange New Worlds, I just couldn’t find the energy to catch up. Maybe someday. I do really like the casting in this series, and Anson Mount is the perfect Pike (though I thought he looked more handsome in the very first episode before he shaved and cut his hair). However, it should be noted that Season 4 has a stellar 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, higher than any previous season. If there is a show that could lure me back to Star Trek, it’s this one.
Silo – Season 3 (Apple TV)
What It’s About: Set in a dystopian future, 10,000 people live in a massive, self-sustaining underground "Silo" comprising 144 levels. Residents are strictly governed by regulations and believe the outside world is toxic, but the protagonist, an engineer named Juliette Nichols, begins to uncover secrets about the Silo’s history and the truth behind their world.
Why You Should Watch: I thought the first season was a bit slow but ended up being a really compelling mystery. For whatever reason, I couldn’t get into Season 2 and still need to catch up. I keep looking at this and Sugar and thinking, I need to watch these shows! But then something else is out that I have to watch. Time is my enemy, and yet the only thing that can defeat my enemy is more of it, which I cannot get. What a conundrum! Season 3 airs weekly on Thursday evenings for a total of 10 episodes, with the finale dropping on September 4.
Lioness – Season 3 (Paramount+)
What It’s About: Taylor Sheridan's Lioness returns for a third season with Zoe Saldaña back as CIA operative Joe McNamara, who finds herself caught up in her most dangerous mission yet. As a sprawling conspiracy threatens both national security and the people she cares about most, Joe is forced to balance her loyalty to the mission with her responsibilities at home. Nicole Kidman, Morgan Freeman, Michael Kelly, Laysla De Oliveira, Genesis Rodriguez, and Dave Annable all return for another season of high-stakes espionage and military action.
Why You Should Watch: You know, I thought the first season of Lioness was pretty excellent military spy thriller fare, and I’m a sucker for that kind of stuff. I’m okay with shows that make Islamic radical terrorists and South American cartels the bad guys and I’m okay with shows that point out that often the bad guys can be right here in the West, too. Taylor Sheridan is a bit more “red-blooded” than a lot of contemporary Hollywood and that’s fine, but I just got kind of sick of the characters in Season 2, so I’m behind. New episodes drop Sundays with the finale landing on September 20.
Ghost in the Shell (Prime Video)
What It’s About: Ghost in the Shell has been around forever, but it’s always fun to see a new take on an old classic. The new series, which debuted on Prime Video this past Tuesday, was created by Science Saru (aka Science Monkey), the studio behind the hit Devilman Crybaby and Danadan. The new series is based on the 1989-91 manage of the same name and takes place in the distant future (well, 2029) in a futuristic Japan replete with elite cyborgs, tactical anti-terrorism forces and mysterious hackers. You can also watch the old 1995 movie on Prime Video. A total of 10 episodes will comprise the first season, with the finale airing on September 8.
Why You Should Watch: If you like this anime series, or you’re just into anime in general, this is probably your thing. I found that even though I’ve seen the movie, I was totally lost and confused after the first episode and so I haven’t continued. Maybe someday.
Stuart Fails To Save The Universe (HBO Max)
What It’s About: Stuart Fails to Save the Universe stars Kevin Sussman, reprising his Big Bang Theory role as Stuart. Comic book store owner Stuart Bloom is tasked with restoring reality after he breaks a device built by Sheldon and Leonard, accidentally bringing about a multiverse Armageddon — and as the title implies, things don't go well. Along the way he meets alternate-universe versions of familiar Big Bang Theory faces.
Why You Should Watch: First, a confession: I have never watched even a single episode of Big Bang Theory. Sure, I’ve seen the odd clip here or there, but I really couldn’t even tell you what it’s about. And yet, this show sounds like a really clever spinoff. It takes the sitcom into an entirely new genre, and even though I’m sick of multiverse stuff, this sounds really fun. It has a 71%/78% critic/audience split on RT. New episodes land Thursdays and the finale drops on September 24.

Wrexham 1-2 Birmingham: Phil Neumann's double extends Red Dragons' winless start to Championship season
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wrexham and Birmingham City at the Racecourse Ground; defender Phil Neumann scored either side of a Callum Doyle equaliser to earn victory for Chris Davies' Blues
Friday 28 August 2026 22:44, UK
Wrexham's winless start to the season was extended to four games in all competitions after they were beaten 2-1 by Birmingham at the Racecourse Ground.
Centre-back Phil Neumann - who has never scored more than two goals in a single season - scored both Blues goals, either side of a Callum Doyle equaliser.
It was the ideal response from Chris Davies' side, following their 6-1 hammering at the hands of Brentford in the Carabao Cup in midweek.
